status: Workbench coming soon. CLI available now.
heroBody: A desktop workspace for the entire model lifecycle. Explore, adapt, evaluate and serve open models with your own data and compute.
heroNote: Open source. Your infrastructure. No account required for the CLI.
previewNote: This is a workbench concept, not a running training job. Training, evaluation and serving are available today through the Soup CLI.
whyTitle: Your model work has outgrown the tabs.
whyBody: A workbench should connect the experiments, the data and the decision to ship.
painSimpleBody: Simple interfaces reach their limit when the task needs real post-training.
painComplexBody: Scripts, notebooks and dashboards scatter the evidence from every run.
painPrivateBody: Sensitive datasets and adapted weights belong on infrastructure you control.
graphLabel: Documents and experiment fragments assemble into a connected graph as you scroll.
graphNote: One place for the context behind your next model.
stationsTitle: From the first prompt to production.
stationsBody: The desktop workbench is in development. Three stations already have a working engine in the open-source CLI.
stationPlaygroundBody: Explore open models before changing them.
stationDataBody: Prepare, clean and label the material your model learns from.
stationPromptsBody: Develop instructions and compare their behaviour.
stationRagBody: Bring relevant documents into the conversation.
stationAgentsBody: Connect model actions and MCP tools.
stationTrainBody: Adapt model weights to your own examples.
stationEvalsBody: Check task quality and regressions before release.
stationDeployBody: Serve a model on compute you control.
ownershipTitle: Your hardware. Your data. Your model.
ownershipBody: Work locally or on cloud GPUs you control. The workbench is being built around the live training, evaluation and serving engine; model work does not pass through Soup infrastructure.
waysBody: Choose the amount of control a task needs. The visual and copilot interfaces are planned; the terminal path works today.
noCodeBody: Choose a model, dataset and recipe. Let the workbench prepare the settings.
copilotBody: Describe the outcome. The copilot coordinates the stations.
codeBody: Keep full control of reproducible commands and configuration.
copilotRequest: Adapt Llama to our support tickets, then check whether it is ready for release.
copilotReply: Plan: prepare the dataset, fine-tune, evaluate. Keep the release verdict and its evidence together.
copilotPlaceholder: Ask about a training, evaluation or deployment task…
conceptOnly: Interface concept · not connected to a model
gateNote: A release decision needs task improvement, preserved general ability and checks against metric gaming.
workflowTitle: Raw data in. A model you can stand behind out.
workflowBody: Explore, prepare, train, evaluate and deploy. Production feedback becomes the next dataset.
verdictBody: A run produces a SHIP or DON'T SHIP decision with an evidence file your team can commit, inspect and re-check.
verdictExample: Example verdict, not a measured result
ctaBody: Install the open-source CLI for fine-tuning, evaluation and serving. The desktop workbench is the next layer.
animationLabel: A rotating field of ASCII characters connects into a model workspace.
